module_title: Peasant and Tribal Uprisings - Basic Understanding
introduction: The British land revenue systems, heavy taxation, and interference in traditional forest rights caused immense suffering among peasants and tribal communities. This led to numerous localized, armed rebellions against the British, Zamindars, and moneylenders during the 18th and 19th centuries.

core_concepts.title: Causes of Tribal Uprisings
core_concepts.description: Tribals (Adivasis) revolted mainly because the British introduced new forest laws restricting their access to forest produce, and outsiders (moneylenders and traders, called 'Dikus') exploited them.

core_concepts.title: Santhal Rebellion (1855-56)
core_concepts.description: Also known as the 'Santhal Hool', it took place in the Rajmahal Hills (Jharkhand). The Santhals rebelled against oppressive Zamindars and moneylenders. It was brutally suppressed by the British.

core_concepts.title: Indigo Revolt (1859-60)
core_concepts.description: A peasant movement in Bengal where farmers refused to grow Indigo under highly exploitative conditions forced by European planters. It was a highly successful, non-violent strike.

core_concepts.title: Munda Rebellion (1899-1900)
core_concepts.description: Led by Birsa Munda in the Chhotanagpur region, this uprising was known as the 'Ulgulan' (Great Tumult). It aimed to drive out the British and establish 'Munda Raj'.

important_entities.name: Sidhu and Kanhu
important_entities.significance: Mobilized thousands of Santhals to fight against the British and the 'Dikus' (outsiders).

important_entities.name: Birsa Munda
important_entities.significance: Declared himself a messenger of God, urged his followers to give up animal sacrifice and alcohol, and led a fierce armed rebellion against colonial exploitation.

important_entities.name: Dinabandhu Mitra
important_entities.significance: Wrote the famous play 'Neel Darpan' (The Indigo Mirror) in 1860, which brilliantly portrayed the plight of the indigo farmers.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Remember the distinction: Peasant revolts were mostly against high taxes and eviction by Zamindars, while Tribal revolts were additionally against the loss of forest rights and cultural interference.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: A quick way to remember the three most frequently asked uprisings in basic exams: Santhal (1855), Indigo (1859), and Munda (1899).

exam_strategy_tips: Always associate the leaders with their respective rebellions (e.g., Sidhu-Kanhu with Santhal, Birsa with Munda).
Questions about 'Neel Darpan' (its author and the revolt it represents) are extremely common.
